about: Where the four load cells sit under the deck, and how to turn their volts into newtons.
Positions are measured on the top surface from the deck's FRONT-LEFT corner (seen from above,
facing forward on the belt): x_m to the right, y_m toward the back, in metres, to the centre
of each load cell. (The positions are still rough: measure them.)
WIRING: load cell N plugs into the amplifier's load-cell input N (M12 connectors 1-4 on the
Michigan Scientific SGA12), so signals NX, NY, NZ come out on wire bundle N. 'serial' is the
Michigan Scientific serial (TR3D-A-3K ###) of the cell at that corner on that input.
SCALE: newtons_per_volt is per axis, from that serial's calibration sheet. The SGA12 has gain
201 and 10 V excitation, so a sheet giving '1 mV/V = L newtons' means newtons_per_volt =
L / 2.01. A negative number flips that axis (the GUI wants a load pressing down to be +Z).
CROSSTALK: rows are what the X, Y, Z channels read, columns the load applied on X, Y, Z,
as a fraction (sheet 'Output (lb)' / applied lb, fitted over +/-3000 lbf). Forces are
corrected by its inverse. Leave it out for no correction.
